source: Zhang, Wan, Yu, Wu, Zhou, Tsang, An (2026) Judged Useless, Queried Anyway: tool-using agents rarely turn their own evidence judgments into stopping decisions
finding: Agents judge a failing source as useless 97-100% of the time but almost never stop because of it. Prompt cues change when they stop, not what they stop on. A harness rule that forces an answer after 5 useless results in a row fixes it.
numbers: Success (mean of 6 failure regimes, 300 questions), none vs enforced rule: Qwen2.5-7B .192 vs .237; Llama-3.1-8B .263 vs .328; Qwen3-8B .448 vs .474; Qwen3-32B .509 vs .572; Claude Haiku 4.5 .501 vs .598; Claude Sonnet 5 .632 vs .653 (first 100 q, p=.051). After 5 useless judgments in a row, unaided Qwen3-8B answers on 1 of 292 questions. Pre-registered replication on 300 fresh questions passed 19 of 19 tests.
quote: Stopping only follows the evidence when the harness enforces an integration step that forces an answer after five consecutive results judged useless.
limits: Retrieval QA with controlled source failures; 7 agents; stop rule is hand-set (5), not learned. Sonnet gain not significant.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for gap 3: a text-only rule outside the model works on closed API models (Haiku +.097). Do not rely on the model to act on its own sufficiency judgment; the scaffold must enforce the stop.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Judged Useless, Queried Anyway (html full text): budget and premature-stop results
finding: A stated budget turns into a quota: weak models answer on the last allowed action. Doubling the budget doubles tool calls with no success gain. Permission to answer from memory or thinking mode causes early stops that ignore evidence.
numbers: Budget-cued 7-8B models answer on the last action in 51-79% of answers on failing sources (FEVER 69-96%). Budget doubled to 16 actions: calls roughly double, no gain; Qwen3-32B +46% calls for no gain. Qwen3-8B with memory permission answers before any real result on 55% of questions where the source recovers after 3 failures. Qwen3-32B thinking mode answers from memory on 97% of failing-source questions (11% without thinking). Enforced rule is non-inferior on recovering or clean sources in 18 of 20 tests (margin -0.05).
limits: A direct premature-stop rate on healthy sources is not in the part read (about 60% of the text). Small open models dominate.
agent_relevance: Gives measured too-early stop numbers by condition for gap 2. A fixed step budget is a bad stop rule: it becomes a quota. Prefer a rule keyed to evidence, and test it on recovering sources too.

source: Han et al. (2026) Your Models Have Thought Enough: Training Large Reasoning Models to Stop Overthinking (JET), arXiv 2509.23392 v3
finding: RL that truncates rollouts at the model's own early-sufficient point and uses a quality-controlled length reward. Models cut length without losing accuracy. An exponential-decay length reward causes premature truncation on hard tasks.
numbers: DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-1.5B: +4.6% accuracy and -46.3% length on Olympiad. 1.5B averages -39.7% length. 7B: AIME24 54.0 (+2.7), AMC 81.0 (+2.1). 8B Llama distill: +2 points, -31% tokens in-domain; -29% out-of-domain. One table row: 52.5 (+5.0) at length -13.0%. Baseline LCR1 on 7B MATH500 cut length over 50% but lost 4.4 points. Laser raised GSM8K tokens by 105.8%.
quote: LRMs have accumulated sufficient information early in reasoning, making further reasoning steps redundant.
limits: Math-trained open distilled models; no direct false-stop rate. The reward design, not the truncation point, is the failure lever.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: an RL stop signal can work if rollouts include truncated short paths and the length reward is gated by correctness. Steep length penalties cut hard items.

source: Dai et al. (2025) S-GRPO: Serial-Group Decaying-Reward Policy Optimization, arXiv 2505.07686
finding: RL on the exit decision. One reasoning path, several exit points; only correct exits are rewarded and reward decays the later the exit. This teaches the model to stop early when safe.
numbers: Qwen3 and DeepSeek-distilled models; GSM8K, AIME 2024, AMC 2023, MATH-500, GPQA Diamond. Sequence length down 35.4% to 61.1%; absolute accuracy gains 0.72% to 6.08%.
limits: Abstract page only; no per-model table read. Math and one science set.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: a correct-only, step-discounted reward (the CaRT objective shape) worked as RL on the stop decision in math, unlike CaRT's binary-reward RL variant that drifted long.

finding: A trajectory classifier plus SFT on self-generated stop signals plus stop-aware GRPO. Large length cuts with accuracy roughly kept, including on a held-out science set.
numbers: Qwen3-8B. ESTAR-LITE (classifier, tau=0.9): USMLE 77.53->76.83, 2412->549 tokens; MATH500 94.0->93.2, 3951->2019; AIME 70.00->66.67, 6123->3045 (95.2% retained). Full ESTAR: MATH500 93.8 at 635 tokens vs AdaptThink 93.8 at 2130. GPQA, trained only on USMLE and deepscaleR: accuracy retained 98.9% to 100.0% across 6 models, length shortened x2.0 to x3.8. Threshold sweep (USMLE): tau .99 gives 77.53% at 463 tokens; tau .80 gives 73.76% at 185 tokens. RL reward 1/4 format + 1/4 stop earliness + 1/2 accuracy.
limits: No stop precision or false-stop rate reported; no error bars; abstract averages do not match the tables; AIME lost 3.3 points.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: the only false-stop proxy is the threshold sweep, where lowering tau trades 3.8 accuracy points for about 2.5x fewer tokens. Gap 9: transfer to a new domain held up here, unlike dermatology in CaRT.

source: Akter, Shihab, Sharma (2025) Anytime-Valid Answer Sufficiency Certificates for LLM Generation via Sequential Information Lift, arXiv 2510.06478 v2
finding: A statistical stop rule that tests whether the output carries enough information versus a weakened baseline, with a bound on premature stops. The guarantee covers information sufficiency, not correctness.
numbers: Length reduction 22-28% vs sequential baselines (body: 23-26% vs SelfCheck, 19-23% vs E-Value). Premature-stop rate at delta=0.1: 0.083 GSM8K, 0.091 HotpotQA; GPT-4o and Llama-3-70B 0.079-0.092. Sufficient-looking but incorrect: 13.2% (ProofWriter) to 22.7% (LegalBench). With a correctness gate: high-lift-but-incorrect 18.5% -> 10.9%, correctness 76.8% -> 83.4%, overhead 12% -> 16%. The gate validates 83% of stops.
quote: EDFL is not a standalone solution for safety-critical domains.
limits: Needs token log-probabilities; the LLM-judge agreement table (appendix S) was beyond the text read, so the 82-87% agreement figure from a web summary is unverified.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 3: a measured false-stop number exists (about 8-9% premature; 11-23% sufficient but wrong). 'Information sufficient' and 'answer correct' are different events; a correctness gate cuts the second error.

source: Shrivastava (2026) Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops, arXiv 2606.27009
finding: For writer-critic loops, stop when consecutive drafts stop changing in meaning (embedding similarity with patience). A per-round LLM judge erased the savings.
numbers: 60 HotpotQA test questions. Judge-free semantic stopper: 38% fewer operational tokens than fixed max_iterations, quality parity (delta Information Score -0.004, p=0.81). Per-round LLM-judge variant called counter-productive. Oracle best-round selection beats every practical policy by +0.115 Information Score (p about 4e-11).
limits: Abstract-level page; small test set; one task type; judge cost figures not given.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 10: cheap embedding convergence stops as well as a judge, with no extra model call. The remaining loss is choosing the best round, not when to stop. Suggests an answer-stability stop in S8, with a judge only on disagreement.

source: Hammar, Alpcan, Lupu (2026) Optimal Stopping of Self-Refining Foundation Models (CDC 2026), arXiv 2608.10729
finding: Models the number of generate-verify-refine rounds as an optimal stopping problem: stop when expected improvement falls below cost. Policies derived and computed by stochastic approximation; more cost-efficient than prior stopping policies on a coding benchmark.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract only; benchmark and models not named on the page.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: independent evidence from code (not medical or math) that a stop rule of the expected-gain-vs-cost form beats prior stopping heuristics. Matches the form in claim K18. It is not a CaRT-style learned judge.

source: Wan et al. (2025) BEACON: Bayesian Optimal Stopping for Efficient LLM Sampling, arXiv 2510.15945
finding: Sequential sampling with a Bayesian posterior over the reward distribution; stop when the expected gain of one more sample is below its cost. No training.
numbers: Up to 80% fewer samples with response quality maintained (abstract).
limits: Abstract only; benchmarks and models not read.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: a training-free sample-level stop with an explicit gain-vs-cost rule; same family as Adaptive-Consistency and ESC.

source: Optimal Stopping vs Best-of-N for inference-time optimization (Pandora's Box), arXiv 2510.01394
finding: Frames sampling as Pandora's Box. A UCB-style stopping rule with an adaptive best-of-N benchmark matches or beats the best fixed N in nearly all of 1,600 profiles.
numbers: Win rate vs fixed Best-of-N at equal average compute above 54% in most cost settings. At acceptance-rate targets 0.75 and above, 15-35% fewer samples than matched fixed-N. Data: AlpacaFarm and HH-RLHF, 100 prompts each; Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen-2.5-7B; 2 reward models; 960 responses per profile.
limits: Authors not read. Reward-model scores, not task correctness. Theory assumes i.i.d. rewards. Main figures show one model.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: a stop rule beats fixed N at EQUAL average compute, the test the critique asked for, though on preference rewards, not reasoning correctness.

source: PeerConf: Self-Calibrating Early Stopping for Efficient Parallel LLM Reasoning (NeurIPS 2026 listing) and MARS (chatpaper listing), via web-search summary only
finding: Per-trace early exit inside a voting run: a trace whose running answer probe clears a threshold commits, casts its vote and frees its seat. The threshold is estimated from traces finishing in the same run. MARS stops the vote when the leader is safe.
numbers: Search summary: PeerConf uses 60.7-79.8% fewer tokens than self-consistency at 32 traces and 23.2-61.3% fewer than DeepConf. MARS: 25-47% of SC tokens saved, 14-29% on top of DeepConf Online, matching full-budget accuracy.
limits: Not opened: the NeurIPS page returned 404. No arXiv id. Numbers are second-hand.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: suggests trace-level and vote-level stops can be stacked. Treat as unverified until the papers are read.

source: Does Your Reasoning Model Implicitly Know When to Stop Thinking? (SAGE / SAGE-RL), arXiv 2602.08354
finding: Claims models already know when to stop but standard sampling hides it. SAGE sampling exposes the stop point; SAGE-RL trains it into pass@1 inference.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page. Claims accuracy and efficiency gains on several mathematical benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Supports the view that the stop signal is latent (probe literature, K06) and that RL can surface it. No false-stop numbers.

source: Zhu, Xie, Rao (2026) Stopping and Routing LLM Judge Panels, arXiv 2608.19802
finding: Stop adding judges when validation gain falls below a threshold. Copy judges add nothing, complements help globally, specialists should be routed.
numbers: No numbers in the abstract. Seven audit domains (reasoning, code, safety, preference, reward-model, summarization, math).
limits: Abstract only; the comparison with a fixed panel size was not read.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: the same stop-when-gain-below-cost form applied to a panel of judges; relevant if our stop judge is itself an ensemble.

source: Negative: id 2503.12434, given in a web summary as a sales-call optimal-stopping paper, is actually a survey of LLM agent optimization (Du et al.)
finding: The id does not match the 'Learning When to Quit in Sales Conversations' paper. The sales-call stopping paper was not located or read.
limits: Id mismatch only. Do not cite the sales-call paper.
agent_relevance: Record that the sales-call stopping agent (LLM imitating a retrospectively inferred optimal stopping policy) is unverified.

source: Negative search: LLM versus human on classic optimal stopping tasks (secretary problem)
finding: arXiv abstract search for 'secretary problem' with LLM returned zero results on 2026-11-03. Two web searches also found no LLM-vs-human secretary or sampling-cost study. LLM optimal-stopping work found is theory or inference-time sampling only (Pandora's Box, BEACON, Hammar et al.).
numbers: 0 arXiv hits for the exact query; 0 for 'when to stop' asking questions LLM interactive information seeking.
limits: Absence of evidence from arXiv search plus web search; behavioural journals and non-arXiv venues were not searched.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open. To close it we must run it: secretary problem and costly-sampling tasks, compare LLM thresholds with the 1/e rule and with the known human tendency to stop early.

source: Agentic XAI case study in decision support for rice cultivation: refinement rounds and LLM-judge stopping, arXiv 2512.21066
finding: Over 11 refinement rounds (0-10), quality peaked at rounds 3-4 and then declined. Judges over-scored by 1.4-2.3 points but ranked rounds like experts.
numbers: Peak gain 30-33% over round 0 for both experts and LLM judges; crop scientists rated final rounds below the starting output. Judge-vs-expert round ranking Spearman rho 0.58-0.90. A web summary said the worst judge was the generating model itself (not confirmed on the abstract page).
limits: Single-domain case study; abstract page only; not a validated stopping algorithm.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 3: refinement past the peak made output worse, so a large fixed budget has a real cost. Screened judges can find the peak but raw scores are inflated. Avoid unscreened self-judging.

source: Learning When to Sample: Confidence-Aware Selective Sampling for Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning, arXiv 2603.08999 v4
finding: Look at one reasoning trajectory using numeric and linguistic features; only if it signals uncertainty, trigger multi-path sampling. Trained on MedQA, transferred to other sets with calibration only.
numbers: Accuracy change -0.41 +/- 0.58 and -0.31 +/- 0.58 points; token reduction 71.7 +/- 5.0% and 36.6 +/- 9.1% vs two multi-path baselines. Transfer without fine-tuning to MathQA, MedMCQA, MMLU.
limits: Abstract only; authors and models not read; which figure maps to which setting is unclear.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1, 6 and 9: a small learned decider on text features transfers across datasets with only calibration, and it chooses at trace level whether to go to vote level. Design target for a cheap text-only judge.

source: Beyond the Commitment Boundary: Probing Epiphenomenal Chain-of-Thought in Large Reasoning Models, arXiv 2606.13603
finding: Answer logits at each step show a commitment point after which later steps do not change the answer probability. Attention probes decode answer-formation stages and allow early exit.
numbers: Up to 55% shorter chain-of-thought when exiting at the commitment boundary with little effect on performance (abstract).
quote: This transition often happens in a single step, well before the model's reasoning block ends.
limits: Abstract only; open weights needed; no false-stop breakdown.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: here 'answer stabilises' is the stop criterion, read from answer logits. It tests stability, not information sufficiency, so it can fire when the model has locked onto a wrong answer.

source: Wang et al. CaRT re-read: counterfactual construction, RL reward, OOD and future-work text, arXiv 2510.08517
finding: Counterfactuals: medical prefixes where one Q-A pair adds 50% or more success are positives; the negative changes only the last Q-A pair so success falls below 30%. Math negatives remove a larger block of steps. OOD dermatology: base and SFT fall below the naive fixed-count stop; CaRT stays above it with a smaller margin. Joint optimisation of what to ask and when to stop is future work, not tested.
numbers: RL variant: binary reward +1 if terminating when success rate is 0.5 or more, or continuing when below 0.5; -1 otherwise (GRPO on top of SFT). Main text test sets: 100 in-distribution and 200 dermatology problems. Removing counterfactuals gives the largest drop; reasoning adds consistent gains; in math, ablating either gives lower success with more tokens.
quote: Future work could jointly optimize what to ask and when to stop.
limits: Labels need an external model's success rate on full and partial context (an oracle with many rollouts). Main results are in figures only.
agent_relevance: Gaps 4, 5, 9: the counterfactual needs a success-rate oracle and is not built from answer-change history. Joint learning is the authors' open claim with no experiment in CaRT. OOD loss is shown only for dermatology.
